public_rationale: The statement contains a checkable numerical assertion, but its margin basis is missing. CoreWeave's filing shows a six-year depreciation policy and illustrates the accounting problem: a ratio above 70% can be calculated while excluding server depreciation recorded elsewhere. It would be unfair to use that ratio as a clean contradiction, or lower EBITDA margins as proof of the ceiling.
limitations: Unknown accounting basis prevents a supported or contradicted financial verdict.
One company's annual accounts cannot establish an industry-wide quarterly ceiling.
The value judgments and hedged obsolescence language are not independently scored.

conditions: assuming consistent payments, tenancy, and six years of depreciation

statement.excerpt: Even if they somehow succeed, these are pathetic businesses with mediocre margins — 70% at best, assuming consistent payments, tenancy, and six fucking years of depreciation to actually break even, which might be difficult considering the yearly upgrade cycle makes the entire thing near-obsolete by the time you’re done paying it off.

from_speaker: six fucking years of depreciation to actually break even
near-obsolete by the time you’re done paying it off
our_interpretation: Assess the numerical margin ceiling and the claimed connection between depreciation and break-even. The descriptions 'pathetic' and 'mediocre' are value judgments.
Gross margin is the most natural reading given the surrounding discussion of gross margins, but the claim does not define which costs it includes.
Use the latest completed reporting quarter generally available before the post, October–December 2025, rather than later operating results.
A six-year accounting useful life does not by itself specify a six-year cash payback period.
The obsolescence clause is hedged and lacks a performance, price or utilization threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable operator or project evidence establishes the asserted margin ceiling under the specified conditions and demonstrates why six-year depreciation is required for break-even.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying operator exceeds 70% on the same defined margin basis, or comparable project economics demonstrate break-even without the asserted six-year requirement.

evidence.locator: Note 2, Property and Equipment; Results of Operations
evidence.explanation: The filing lists a six-year technology-equipment life, but records server depreciation in technology and infrastructure expense. Subtracting only reported cost of revenue produces a 71.68% annual ratio; that excludes relevant costs and covers a different period, so it is not a decisive counterexample.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defined margin measure and matching project or operator evidence, plus a model connecting depreciation assumptions to break-even.
